newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares lower at noon as caution returns.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares lower at noon as caution returns.

text.p: Shenzhen B shares edged lower in thin trading on Tuesday morning as investors remained jittery over the recent government crackdown on speculative trading, traders said.
The foreign currency B share index slipped 0.69 points or 0.46 percent to 150.08, after hitting an intra-session high of 153.47, on turnover of HK$55.5 million.
The domestic currency A share index fell 8.13 points or 1.82 percent to 437.52 on turnover of 2.6 billion yuan.
"We are hearing a lot of negative rumours, including one of a possible government announcement to punish brokerages accused of irregularities," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
In May, the markets reacted sharply to talk that Beijing would ban four of China's biggest brokerages from trading on their own accounts and fine them for alleged trading misconduct.
On the B share market, the biggest loser was pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda which fell HK$0.33 or 6.56 percent to HK$4.70.
Beijing Orient Electronics Group Co debuted on Shenzhen's B share market on Tuesday and ended the morning at HK$4.10 compared with an offer price of HK$3.08.
The newcomer's gains were limited by weak market sentiment after recent government measures aimed at squeezing bank funds out of the stock markets, traders said.
Beijing last week ordered all state banks to unwind their stock market positions within 10 sessions to reduce the flow of "hot money", or speculative funds, into China's heated markets.
Banks were also ordered to stop trading on the treasury debt repurchase market, through which large amounts of bank funds were channelled into the equity markets.
The ban followed recent moves to bar state and listed firms from speculative stock trading.
